 JUDGMENT The petitioners have filed this Petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the Death of one Puttalingappa in a road traffic accident dated 15.03.2024.
MFCSCCH-25 2

. The case of the Petitioners in brief is that:
On 15.03.2024 at about 7.30 to 7.40pm the deceased was proceeding by walk on Sri.Ranga Kalyana Mantapa to RT Nagar Education Institute on the extreme left side of the road in order to get to his home.

While deceased was crossing the road, infront of Manak Marble and Granite Shop, Doddaballapura-Yelahanka Road, suddenly a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EB-0929 came with high speed, ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner with excessive speed and dashed to the deceased.
Due to the said accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries to head and other parts of the body.

3. The petitioners further averred that, immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Navachethana Hospital at Yelahanka, wherein he has taken treatment and later shifted to Baptist Hospital, Bangalore, thereafter for higher treatment as per the advice of the doctor he was shifted to Yelahanka Govt. Hospital, but in spite of best treatment given in the said hospital, Puttalingappa died at MFCSCCH-25 the said hospital due to accidental injuries on 16.03.2023 at about 1.15am.
The post mortem examination was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
So far the petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, funeral and obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

Due to the sudden and sad demise of the deceased in the Narasamma vs Shiva Kumar .M on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98795001/
2 tragic accident, the petitioners are undergoing deep mental shock, pain and sufferings.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. The petitioners further stated that, prior to the date of accident, he was hale and healthy, working as a Watchman and earning more than Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to untimely death of the deceased petitioners life has become dark, miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
Petitioners being the wife and children of the deceased Puttalingappa have undergone severe shock.

5. The accident is due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EB-0929 and the Rajanukunte Police have registered a case in MFCSCCH-25 Cr.
NO.0076/2024 for the offences punishable u/Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC.
The respondent being the RC owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
6. In response to the service of notice, the Respondent did not appear before this court hence, placed ex-parte.

7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following Points:
1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.Puttalingappa.?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sri.Puttalingappa had died due to the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 15.03.2024 at about 7.30 to 7.40pm Manak Marble and Granite, Singanayakanahalli, Yelahanka Taluk and Hobli,
Bangalore, due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EB-0929 as alleged?
3.
Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation as claimed?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What Order or Award?
MFCSCCH-25 8.

In order to prove their case, the Petitioners have examined Petitioner No.1 - Smt. Narasamma - Wife of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.10.
9.
Heard both the Counsels and perused the materials on record.

10. My finding to the above issues are as follows:-
 Point No.1 : In the affirmative  Point Nos.2 & 3 : In the affirmative,
Point No.4 :

As per final order for  the Following:
Narasamma vs Shiva Kumar .M on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98795001/
3  REASONS  11. Point No.1:
It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner Nos.2 to 5 are the major sons and daughters of the deceased - Puttalingappa.
The Petitioners to prove their relationship have examined the 1 st Petitioner as PW.1.
PW.1 has specifically spoken about this relationship in her chief-examination.
Apart from that, to prove the relationship, the Petitioners have produced their Notarized MFCSCCH-25 copies of Aadhar Cards as per Ex.P.10.

In Ex.P.10 - Aadhar Card of the petitioner No.1, her husband's name is mentioned as Puttalingappa and in the Aadhar Cards of the petitioner Nos.2 & 3, their father's name is mentioned as Puttalingappa.

In the Aadhar Cards of the petitioner No.4 her husband's name is mentioned as Shivaraju Y.H. and in the same manner in the Aadhar Card of the Petitioner No.5, her husband's name is mentioned as Harisha.
The petitioners have also produced Ex.P.6 Inquest Mahazar, in this documents all the petitioners names are mentioned as wife and children of Puttalingappa.
These documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances,
relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and the documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner Nos.1 to 5 are the Wife and children of the deceased.
Accordingly, Point No.1 is held in the affirmative.

MFCSCCH-25 12. Point No.2:
The Petitioners to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Motorcycle have examined Petitioner No.1 as PW.1 and produced documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.9.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in her affidavit filed in lieu of her chief examination.
On the other side, the Respondent did not appear before this court hence, placed exparte.

13. The documents produced by the Petitioners such as the FIR in Cr.No.0076/2024 of Rajanukunte Police on the Complaint of the deceased's son and registered on 16.03.2024, Spot Mahazar, spot sketch, Accident Inspection Report, Notice to the RC owner of the offending vehicle and reply,
Inquest mahazar, PM report, charge sheet and the statement of witnesses as per Exs.P.1 to P.9 are all public documents and have initial presumptive value under law.
These documents fully and completely corroborate with the evidence of PW.1.

The investigation officer in crime MFCSCCH-25 No.0076/2024 of Rajanukunte Police has conducted the investigation in detail and has filed the charge sheet against the rider of the offending Motorcycle bearing No.KA-50-EB- 0929 holding that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending Motorcycle.
There is no cross examination to PW.1 since, the respondent did not appear before this court.
14. The Inquest mahazar produced as per Ex.P.6 and PM report produced as per Ex.P.7 clearly show that 'Death is due to SHOCK & HEMORRHAGE as a result of multiple injuries sustained.

Therefore,
Narasamma vs Shiva Kumar .M on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98795001/
4
I hold that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the rider of the offending Motorcycle.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.2 in the Affirmative.
15. Point No.3:
PW.1 has specifically spoken before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, they have lost the bread earner of their family and their loving father.
He has MFCSCCH-25 further deposed that they have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, conveyance, transportation of dead body and for performing the funeral ceremonies.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation as per the following discussion.
Monthly income 16.

According to the Petitioners, the deceased was doing Watchman work and earning Rs.30,000/-
per month.
The Petitioners to prove the income of the deceased have not produced any documents such as Pay slips, Bank Statement etc., nor have they examined any witness.
The accident occurred in the year 2024.

Under such circumstances, this court has to consider the income at Rs.16,500/-
notionally for calculating the compensation.
Age of the deceased 17.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar Card of the deceased at Ex.P.10.
As per Ex.P.10, deceased birth year was 1963.
The accident occurred in the year 2024.
This is a public MFCSCCH-25 document and has got presumptive value under law.
This shows that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 61 years.
Therefore, his age is considered as 61 years.
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE PROSPECTS:-
As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 7.

entities.text: Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the deceased has a wife-petitioner No.1 aged about 47 years, Two major sons - Petitioner Nos.2 & 3 aged about 31 & 27 years and Two Major married daughters.
On the basis of Aadhar Card, it can be seen that both sons are major and both daughters are married and settled.
Therefore, they are not considered as the dependents of the deceased.
Only petitioner No.1 is the dependent of the deceased.

18. As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others (AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged about above 60 years are MFCSCCH-25 not entitled to any future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others (AIR 2017 S.C 5157)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the Sarala Verma case, if there is a sole dependent then 1/2 of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses, balance comes to Rs.8,250/-.

Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.6,93,000/- (Rs.8,250/- X 7 x 12) =
Rs.6,93,000/-).
Narasamma vs Shiva Kumar .M on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98795001/
5 ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:-
In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130

entities.text: Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".

19. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. MFCSCCH-25 Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
20.

entities.text: United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. MFCSCCH-25 Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The 1st Petitioner is the wife and as she has lost her husband and companion at the age of 47 years and she has to the live remaining part of her life without him, she is entitled to a sum of Rs.48,000/- under the head of loss of consortium.
Similarly, the petitioner Nos.2 to 4 are the sons and daughters of the deceased, they lost their loving, care taking father.
Therefore, they are also entitled to Rs.48,000/- each, in total Rs.2,40,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of consortium.

iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES:-
PW.1/Petitioner has stated that she has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, funeral expenses and obsequies etc..
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any bills pertaining to the above said expenses.
However, there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.
Therefore, in the MFCSCCH-25 interest of justice, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF ESTATE:-
As mentioned above, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.16,500/- per month.
Out of this, he was spending 1/2 of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
As such, in total, the Petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.9,73,000/-.

LIABILITY 2 1 . T h e r e s p o n d e n t b e i n g t h e R C o w n e r o f t h e o f f e n d i n g m o t o r c y c l e b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-50-EB-0929 hence, liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Though the Petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000, but Petitioners are entitled only for a sum of Rs.9,73,000/- along with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs MFCSCCH-25 to be allowed.
Accordingly I answer Point No.3 in the affirmative.

Narasamma vs Shiva Kumar .M on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98795001/
6 22. Point No.4:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.9,73,000/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Seventy Three Thousand only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent is liable to pay compensa- tion to the petitioners within 60 days from the date of this Judgment.

MFCSCCH-25 On deposit of the award amount and inter- est, Rs.48,000/- each shall be released to the pe- titioner Nos.2 to 5 and Rs.3,00,000/- shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner No.1 for a period of 3 years in any Bank of her choice and the remaining amount shall be released to the petitioner No.1 by way of e-payment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
